mismatches.bugReason: Pinned emails from Microsoft Outlook were migrated successfully during Outlook-to-Outlook migration, but the pin status was not preserved and the emails appeared as normal mails in the destination mailbox due to pinning being a client/UI-specific property that is not supported by migration metadata mapping.

fixSuggestion.suggestion: Implement a mapping to set a separate flag or custom field for pinned email status during migration.
steps: Review the source system's representation of pinned emails and identify any meta-information.
Introduce a migration logic to detect pinned status and translate it into a custom field or tag on the destination.
Update migration documentation to include this mapping as part of the process.
Test the new logic with both Outlook-to-Outlook and Gmail-to-Outlook migrations to ensure proper handling.

mismatches.bugReason: Pinned emails from Microsoft Outlook were migrated successfully during Outlook-to-Outlook migration, but the pin status was not preserved and the emails appeared as normal mails in the destination mailbox due to pinning being a client/UI-specific property that is not supported by migration metadata mapping.

fixSuggestion.suggestion: Implement a workaround to document pin status in a custom email header for future retrieval.
steps: Identify emails with a pin status during the migration process.
Add a custom header (e.g., X-Pinned: true) to these emails before sending them to the destination.
On the client-side, use this header to apply the pin display property in the email client UI.

fixSuggestion.suggestion: Create a distinct label mapping for 'All Mail' drafts to ensure accurate draft count migration.
steps: Identify drafts specifically labeled under 'All Mail' as opposed to other Gmail system labels.
Implement a mapping configuration that explicitly tracks messages in 'All Mail' as part of both a label and their respective folder.
Test the new mapping strategy with a small set of messages to verify draft counts match.

Manually test the folder mapping setup by migrating a single message to ensure it reaches the 'Inbox' folder.
Retry the entire migration process after confirming the folder mapping configuration is correct.

mismatches.bugReason: “All Mail” in Gmail is not a real folder—it is a collection view of all emails across labels (Inbox, Sent, Archive, etc.). Since migration tools work on actual folders/labels, there is no direct “All Mail” folder to migrate.

fixSuggestion.suggestion: Create a distinct label mapping for 'All Mail' drafts to ensure accurate draft count migration.
steps: Identify drafts specifically labeled under 'All Mail' as opposed to other Gmail system labels.
Implement a mapping configuration that explicitly tracks messages in 'All Mail' as part of both a label and their respective folder.
Test the new mapping strategy with a small set of messages to verify draft counts match.

mismatches.bugReason: Folder message count mismatch — messages were not migrated to destination.

fixSuggestion.suggestion: Verify folder mapping configuration and retry the migration process.
steps: Check the migration tool's folder mapping configuration to ensure 'INBOX' is correctly mapped to 'Inbox'.
Review log files for any errors specific to folder mapping during the migration process.
Manually test the folder mapping setup by migrating a single message to ensure it reaches the 'Inbox' folder.
Retry the entire migration process after confirming the folder mapping configuration is correct.

fixSuggestion.suggestion: Modify the migration tool to map Gmail's 'All Mail' to an equivalent virtual folder or label that does not alter the draft or email counts.
steps: Analyze the existing folder mapping logic in the migration tool.
Introduce a virtual layer for 'All Mail' that aggregates messages without creating a conflicting physical folder.
Ensure that the aggregation accounts for drafts and other special label counts.
Test the updated mapping with different Gmail account configurations to verify accurate draft counts post-migration.

Re-attempt migrating the missing messages specifically to ensure they are moved to the correct destination folder.

mismatches.bugReason: “All Mail” in Gmail is not a real folder—it is a collection view of all emails across labels (Inbox, Sent, Archive, etc.). Since migration tools work on actual folders/labels, there is no direct “All Mail” folder to migrate.

fixSuggestion.suggestion: Modify the migration tool to map Gmail's 'All Mail' to an equivalent virtual folder or label that does not alter the draft or email counts.
steps: Analyze the existing folder mapping logic in the migration tool.
Introduce a virtual layer for 'All Mail' that aggregates messages without creating a conflicting physical folder.
Ensure that the aggregation accounts for drafts and other special label counts.
Test the updated mapping with different Gmail account configurations to verify accurate draft counts post-migration.

mismatches.bugReason: Folder message count mismatch — messages were not migrated to destination.

fixSuggestion.suggestion: Ensure correct folder mapping and check for any migration throttling issues.
steps: Verify the folder/label mapping rules between Gmail and Outlook to ensure the source 'INBOX' is correctly mapped to the destination 'Inbox'.
Check migration logs for any errors or warnings related to throttling that may have interrupted message migration.
Inspect the migration configuration for any incorrect settings that may limit the number of messages transferred.
Re-attempt migrating the missing messages specifically to ensure they are moved to the correct destination folder.

mismatches.summaryLine: SENT → Sent Items: expected 15 vs actual 0
mismatches.bugReason: Folder message count mismatch — messages were not migrated to destination.

fixSuggestion.suggestion: Check for incorrect folder mapping configuration for the 'SENT' folder.
steps: Review the mapping configuration to ensure 'SENT' is correctly mapped to 'Sent Items'.
Verify the user's permissions and access rights to the source 'SENT' folder.
Run a test migration of just the 'SENT' folder to ensure messages are synced correctly.
Check destination server logs for any errors related to message delivery to the 'Sent Items' folder.
